strengths: Extremely thorough empirical validation: disjoint selection/evaluation prompt sets, multiple independent LLM judges, multiple random seeds, and quality (incoherence/refusal) tracking alongside safety metrics, which guards against trivial explanations like blanket refusal or generic output degradation.

Strong ablation suite that isolates the causal contribution of the method: random-latent and Stage-1-only ('Top-Delta') baselines fail to replicate the effect, sign-shuffling and one-sided variants weaken it, and layer-choice ablations (layer 20 vs. final layer) support the claim that intermediate-depth, signed, feature-specific constraints are doing the causal work rather than some generic regularization effect.

Comprehensive comparison against relevant baselines (KL regularization, inoculation prompting, preventative steering, test-time steering) showing a consistently better safety-utility Pareto frontier across six domains.

Cross-domain and cross-model generalization checks (latents discovered on Finance transfer to five other domains; full pipeline replicated on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct) that substantially strengthen the generality claims beyond a single setup.

Commendably honest characterization of a failure mode (misalignment re-emergence under prolonged training) with a genuine mechanistic investigation (activation patching, SAE reconstruction checks, residual steering-capacity analysis) rather than hiding or downplaying the limitation.

Practical reproducibility contribution: released latent sets for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct that let practitioners skip the feature-discovery phase, plus detailed appendices specifying hyperparameters, prompts, and judge rubrics.
weaknesses: The final evaluation and core misalignment prompt sets are quite small (29 and 44 prompts respectively), which raises concerns about the statistical reliability of percentage-based misalignment/incoherence estimates, even though SEM across seeds/domains is reported.

The method depends on already possessing (or being able to cheaply produce) a misaligned checkpoint Mmis for model-diffing before latent discovery; while released latent sets partially mitigate this, the general applicability to novel domains/models without such a reference checkpoint is not deeply explored.

Reliance on only two LLM judges (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct) for all misalignment/coherence/adherence scoring introduces potential systematic judge bias that is not independently validated against human annotation.

The core experimental setting (fine-tuning models to produce deliberately incorrect/harmful in-domain advice) is somewhat artificial; it is unclear how well the intervention and its trade-offs transfer to more realistic scenarios where the target fine-tuning behavior is itself benign but narrow.

The central limitation—misalignment re-emergence under extended training—is not resolved, only partially mitigated (via an expanded latent set), leaving open how practical the method is for realistic multi-epoch training regimes.

The pipeline involves numerous heuristic design choices and hyperparameters (candidate pool sizes, incoherence budgets, steering grids, ranking scores, multiple Stage-3 variants), and while ablations show robustness to many of these, the overall procedure remains fairly complex and compute-intensive relative to simpler baselines like KL regularization.
Experiments use LoRA fine-tuning exclusively; it is unclear whether the same blocking mechanism and trade-offs hold under full-parameter fine-tuning, which is common in some deployment settings.
